title: List Rendering: v-for
description: Render arrays and objects dynamically with the powerful v-for directive.

slides.title: v-for Basics
slides.content:
# Looping with `v-for` Use `v-for` to render a list of items based on an array: ```html
  • {{ item }}
    • ``` You can also get the index: ```html
  • {{ index }}: {{ item }}
    • ```

slides.title: Rendering an Array
slides.content: Here's a simple todo list rendered with `v-for`:
slides.codeSnippet: • {{ idx + 1 }}. {{ todo.text }}

slides.title: The Importance of :key 🗝️
slides.content:
Always use `:key` with `v-for`. It gives Vue a hint to track each node's identity, improving performance and avoiding weird bugs. ```html
  • {{ item.name }}
    • ``` If your items don't have a unique ID, use the index as a last resort.

slides.title: v-for with Objects
slides.content:
You can also iterate over object properties: ```html
  • {{ key }}: {{ value }} (index {{ index }})
    • ``` Order is based on `Object.keys()` enumeration.

quizData.question: Why is it important to use a `:key` with `v-for`?

options.text: It's required for the template to compile
It helps Vue track each node's identity for efficient updates
It adds a unique CSS class

quizData.explanation: `:key` gives Vue a hint to reuse and reorder existing elements, which improves performance and prevents rendering issues.
